subject: Re: Phased Capacity Delivery & Annual Prepay Split — invoice triggers
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Park <emma@catalystlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Phased capacity delivery proposal and invoice options

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the call today. Per our discussion I attached a first-pass ramp schedule for Dedicated capacity (CSV/XLSX) showing a phased GPU + TPM commit across 3 tranches over 12 months. High-level options inside the sheet:

- Annual prepay (one invoice) with steeper term discount
- Annual prepay split into 2 installments (50/50) with slight discount reduction
- Multi-year (3yr) prepay with additional price protection and capacity hold-back clauses

Questions for you:
1) Do you need the prepay to be invoiced upfront or is splitting across fiscal quarters acceptable?
2) Any internal procurement constraints for multi-year commitments (e.g., PO cadence, approval windows)?

Attachment: Catalyst_Ramp_Schedule_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Happy to jump on another 30m to walk through.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

From: Emma Park <emma@catalystlabs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Catalyst Labs Procurement <procure@catalystlabs.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Phased capacity delivery proposal and invoice options

Kimberly —

Thanks for the deck & schedule. A few clarifying points from our side after reviewing with finance/procurement:

- We prefer not to fund a full-year prepay in a single invoice at this scale. Can you accommodate a 2-installment annual prepay (50% at signing, 50% at month 6)?
- If we do a 3-year commit, what is the delta in effective discount vs single-year prepay? Need an example TCO table.
- For ramp milestones: our ops team wants the first tranche (25% of reserved capacity) available within 30 days of PO acceptance, then 40% by month 6, remainder by month 12. Is that achievable?

Also attaching a short note from procurement about PO lead time and invoice approvals.

Attachment: Catalyst_Ramp_Schedule_feedback.xlsx

Thanks — Emma
Emma Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Catalyst Labs
emma@catalystlabs.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Park <emma@catalystlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-23T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Phased capacity delivery proposal and invoice options

Emma — thanks for the detailed feedback. Quick responses inline: 

- 2-installment annual prepay: yes, we can do a split 50/50 (signing / month 6) as an option. We typically apply a modest discount adjustment (~3 percentage points off the single-invoice prepay rate) to account for payment timing.

- 3-year commit delta: a 3yr upfront prepay vs 1yr upfront typically yields ~12% effective discount in our examples; 1yr upfront is ~8% nominal. I'll produce a short TCO table showing effective $/token and amortized cost across the three models.

- Delivery milestones: the ops plan you suggest (25% @30d, 40% @6mo, 35% @12mo) is feasible on our side, provided PO & initial payment clear before the first tranche. We'll include SLA start dates tied to tranche completion.

I'm attaching a draft SOW that mirrors those milestones and lists acceptance criteria per tranche. Also preparing a CSV with invoice timing scenarios for finance.

Attachment: SOW_draft_v2.pdf

If acceptable, we can send a final proposal with exact dollar schedules and the invoice cadence for legal review.

Best,
Kim

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-24T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Phased capacity delivery proposal and invoice options — pricing check

Kim / Ben —

Looping you in so we can confirm the commercial levers before we lock a proposal. Notes: 

- Discount floor: recommend we do not go below 9% effective for a one-year upfront prepay; for 3yr upfront we can stretch to 12.5% if we include a modest capacity hold-back clause (we release 85% immediately, 15% as optional reserve).
- Installment pricing: 50/50 split should carry a 3% haircut vs one-time prepay as Kim noted. Finance prefers 30-day net on the second installment once tranche 2 is delivered.
- Risk: if customer significantly front-loads usage, we need clear eviction/burst policy and overage rates.

I'll draft the margin-impact table and share by EOD so Kimberly can close the loop with Catalyst.

-Marissa
VP, Commercial Finance | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Park <emma@catalystlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Catalyst Labs Procurement <procure@catalystlabs.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Phased capacity delivery proposal and invoice options

Emma / Procurement team —

Appreciate the patience while we validated internal pricing. Here is the commercial proposal we can commit to: 

Option A — 1yr Annual Prepay (single invoice at signing)- Effective discount: 8.5%- Delivery: 25% @30d, 40% @6mo, 35% @12mo- SLA start: tranche-specific, 30d/6mo/12mo triggers- Invoicing: single invoice at signing

Option B — 1yr Prepay (2-installment) — Customer-preferred- Effective discount: 5.5% (3pt reduction vs single invoice)- Invoicing: 50% at signing, 50% at month 6 (30-day payment terms on second installment)- Delivery: same tranche milestones, tranche 1 available within 30d of cleared first payment

Option C — 3yr Prepay (upfront)- Effective discount: 12.0%- Delivery: Year 1 baseline (as above) + commit to priority capacity routing and price protection through Year 3- Optional 15% capacity hold-back that can be released on 30d notice (helps us manage cluster capacity)

Other terms:
- Overage: standard per-token overage at published rates; we can add a blended capped overage for Enterprise customers on a case-by-case basis.
- Invoicing mechanics: we can accept a PO and issue invoice upon signature; for the split annual option we will invoice the second installment at month 6, net 30.
- Acceptance: We will attach tranche acceptance criteria to the SOW (performance samples, throughput tests).

I attached a short CSV demonstrating cashflow & amortized $/token under each option. If this is acceptable, we can route the SOW to your legal and procurement teams for final review.

Attachment: Invoice_Term_Scenarios.csv

Next steps: please confirm preferred option (A/B/C) and whether Catalyst wants the 50/50 split. Once confirmed we'll send the final SOW + invoice schedule.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Catalyst Labs Procurement <procure@catalystlabs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Park <emma@catalystlabs.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Phased capacity delivery proposal and invoice options

Hi Kimberly —

Catalyst confirms Option B (1yr prepay, 2-installment) pending receipt of final SOW and invoice schedule. Procurement notes: second installment invoice should be dated to month 6 with net 30; we will raise PO within 5 business days of signed SOW. One ask: please include a short clause in the SOW that clarifies the release process for the second tranche in the event of a delay in payment approval (we need clarity on hold/release mechanics).

Attachment expected: final SOW (PDF)

Thanks — we look forward to the SOW so legal can review.

Procurement Team
Catalyst Labs
